name: What is the typical lifespan of a new roof, and how does that affect my estimate?

mainEntity.name: What is the typical lifespan of a new roof, and how does that affect my estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: The typical lifespan of a new roof varies significantly based on the material chosen. Standard asphalt shingle roofs generally last 20-30 years, while higher-grade architectural shingles or metal roofs can last 40-70 years or more. This lifespan directly affects your estimate, as materials with longer warranties and greater durability typically have a higher upfront cost but may offer better long-term value. We factor material lifespan into our recommendations.
acceptedAnswer.description: New roof lifespan varies by material (e.g., asphalt 20-30 years, metal 40-70+ years); this durability affects the upfront estimate cost.
